Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Conversation, family & daily routines

no adverb

the answer to a question

also no (answer), no, I don’t, no, it isn’t, no, certainly not, no indeed, heck no, not at all

classical

Ter. Eun. 850–853: Satin' id tibi placet? — Nōn.
Plaut. Cas. 231: Manē. — Nōn maneō.
Cic. Ac. 2.104: aut etiam aut nōn respondēre (Lewis & Short s.v. nōn)
Traupman 250

nōn

adverb; mostly with the verb of the question repeated

no, not

Latin has no single word for “no”. The plainest answer repeats the verb with nōn (“Are you staying? — I’m not staying”), or is nōn alone, Cicero’s pair to etiam (see yes).

Other words

  • minimē — no, not at all

    also used · classical · Ter. Hec. 5.3.16: Sed cessās? — Minimē equidem (Lewis & Short s.v. parvus); Traupman 250

    The emphatic negative answer, “by no means”; stronger still minimē gentium (see no way!).

  • minimē vērō — no, certainly not

    also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.10: An tū haec nōn crēdis? — Minimē vērō. (Lewis & Short s.v. parvus); Traupman 250; Traupman 121; Traupman 22: minimē vērō hercle!, heck no!; Traupman 56; Traupman 327

  • immō — no, rather …; on the contrary

    adverb, followed by the correction · also used · classical · Plaut. Most. 3.1.19: Etiam fatētur dē hospite? — Immō pernegat. (Lewis & Short); Traupman 250

    Lewis & Short: never, like minimē, an answer on its own; it brings the clause that corrects the question (see actually).

Examples

  • Dīc mihi, aufūgistīne? — Era, factum. — Satin' id tibi placet? — Nōn.

    Tell me, did you run away? — Yes, ma’am. — Are you pleased with that? — No.Ter. Eun. 850–853

  • Satin' sīc est? — Nōn. — Quid sī sīc? — Propemodum. — Quid sī sīc? — Sat est.

    Is this all right? — No. — How about this? — Nearly. — And this? — That’ll do.Ter. Ph. 210–211

  • quō nunc abīs? — Mitte mē. — Manē. — Nōn maneō. — At pol ego tē sequar.

    where are you off to now? — Let me go. — Stay. — I won’t. — Then I’ll follow you.Plaut. Cas. 231–231e

  • An tū haec nōn crēdis? — Minimē vērō.

    Don’t you believe this? — Certainly not.Cic. Tusc. 1.10 (Lewis & Short s.v. parvus)

  • Vigilatne nunc Olīvia? — Minimē edepol!

    Is Olivia awake now? — Heck no!Traupman 35

See also yes, no way!, actually, no, thank you, is it …?, no.
